text:
anya: Heads-up: site build failed linkcheck on /examples/llm-pipelines#streaming-and-batching. The heading exists but the HTML id is missing the word 'batching'. Strange: the MD heading reads: `## Streaming and\nBatching` (wrapped line in editor).

tom: Ah, line-wrapped headings! Some editors hard-wrap long headings at 80 cols inserting a hard newline. MDX/Docusaurus will treat that as a heading with an inline line break which slugifies differently (it joins lines without a hyphen). Legacy slugify replaced the newline with a space which became a hyphen. So we get two different slugs.

kevin: Repro locally:
```bash
# simulate wrapped heading
printf "## Streaming and\nBatching\n\nSome text" > /tmp/wrap.md
node ./scripts/docusaurus-slugify.js "$(sed -n '1p' /tmp/wrap.md)"
node ./scripts/legacy-slugify.js "$(sed -n '1p' /tmp/wrap.md)"
```
I see docusaurus -> "streaming-andbatching" and legacy -> "streaming-and-batching". Ugh.

anya: That explains several support tickets where old guides linked `#streaming-and-batching` and now 404. Proposed fixes: 1) normalize headings by joining wrapped lines with a single space before slug generation; 2) add a docs lint that warns on hard-wrapped heading lines (editor wrap) and suggests a single-line heading or explicit HTML anchor; 3) generate redirects for anchors with inbound hits.

tom: Agree. Also add a small transform in the migration pipeline: collapse newline sequences inside ATX heading lines to a single space (but only inside the same heading block). We should avoid changing prose elsewhere. I'll sketch a sed/perl one-liner and include test cases.

kevin: Example transform (proof-of-concept):
```bash
perl -0777 -pe "s/^(#{1,6}\\s+)([\\s\\S]*?)(\\n\\n)/$1.(join ' ', split /\\n+/', $2)." -i docs/examples/llm-pipelines.md
```
I'll refine into a safe node script with tests.

anya: For redirects, let's only emit mappings where inbound-links analytics shows traffic (we still have the old-site CSV). Otherwise redirect table explodes.

kevin: Also add a unit test for headings with explicit HTML tags, emoji, and wrapped lines so we exercise edge cases. We should run the slug-compare job in CI for any PR touching docs/*.

docs-bot: New PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5882 by tom 1 collapse wrapped heading lines + warn-lint + slug-compare CI job

ci-bot: docs-ci (slug-compare) queued. Note: job will compare docusaurus vs legacy slug outputs and fail if mismatches found.

anya: Thanks — once PR merges we'll re-run prod linkcheck. If anyone spots other wrapped headings (search for `\n` inside heading lines or grep for '## .*\\n'), paste files here and I'll triage. :rocket:
